newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama aids Colombian regufees, probes deaths.
newsitem.headline: Panama aids Colombian regufees, probes deaths.

text.p: Panama handed out emergency aid on Monday to hundreds of fleeing Colombian refugees and opened an investigation into five deaths, a government official said.

"About 200 refugees have fled to Port Obaldia from violence between Colombian guerrilla and paramilitary groups," Roberto Velasquez, head of Panama's National Civil Protection Service, told reporters.
"Humanitarian aid consists of food, clothes, and medicine. We also found five dead, it's a serious situation," he added.

Velasquez said most of the dead were found over the weekend and appeared to have been killed on Panamanian soil by right-wing death squads, but police were still investigating. He said the refugees, mainly women and children, fled to Port Obaldia, a small port city on Panama's border with Colombia.
Over the years, thousands of Colombian refugees have fled violence in banana-producing Uraba province along Panama's border. Most are repatriated after receiving humanitarian aid.

The area has long been rife with violence as leftist guerrillas and right-wing paramilitary groups vie for power. In recent weeks, the Colombian army has waged an offensive against Marxist rebels there in a bid to cut off what it says are lucrative arms and drug trafficking routes in and out of Colombia via Panama.
